:::{#thm-normal-affine}

#### Gaussian distributions are closed under affine transformations

If $X \sim \ndist{\mean, \ss}$ and $a \ne 0$, then $aX + b \sim \ndist{a\mean + b, a^2\ss}$.

:::

::: proof

Let $Y = aX + b$ and let $f$ be the [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) of $X$.
The [CDF](random-variables.qmd#def-cdf) of $Y$ is
$\cdf_Y\paren{y} = \Pr(aX + b \le y)$.
The density $f$ is continuous everywhere, so at every $y$ the derivative of $\cdf_Y\paren{y}$ is the density of $Y$ by
[the derivative of the CDF is the density](random-variables.qmd#thm-cdf-derivative-is-density),
once $\cdf_Y\paren{y}$ is written through the CDF $\cdf_X$ of $X$.
There are two cases, by the sign of $a$.

- **Case $a > 0$.**
  Dividing by $a > 0$ keeps the order of an inequality, so:

  $$
  \ba
  \cdf_Y\paren{y}
  &= \Pr\paren{X \le \frac{y-b}{a}}
  && \text{(} aX + b \le y \iff X \le (y-b)/a \text{)} \\
  &= \cdf_X\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  && \text{(definition of the CDF)}
  \ea
  $$

  The [chain rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-derivatives.html#thm-chain-rule) gives the derivative:

  $$
  \deriv{y} \cdf_Y\paren{y}
  = \frac{1}{a} f\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  = \frac{1}{\abs{a}} f\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  \quad \text{(} \abs{a} = a \text{)}
  $$

- **Case $a < 0$.**
  Dividing by $a < 0$ reverses the order of an inequality, and $\Pr(X = x) = 0$ for a continuous $X$, so:

  $$
  \ba
  \cdf_Y\paren{y}
  &= \Pr\paren{X \ge \frac{y-b}{a}}
  && \text{(} aX + b \le y \iff X \ge (y-b)/a \text{)} \\
  &= 1 - \cdf_X\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  && \text{(complement, and } \Pr(X = (y-b)/a) = 0 \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

  The chain rule gives the derivative:

  $$
  \deriv{y} \cdf_Y\paren{y}
  = -\frac{1}{a} f\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  = \frac{1}{\abs{a}} f\paren{\frac{y-b}{a}}
  \quad \text{(} \abs{a} = -a \text{)}
  $$

In both cases, $Y$ has density $\p(Y=y) = f\paren{(y-b)/a} / \abs{a}$.
Substitute the Gaussian density of $X$:

$$
\ba
\p(Y=y)
&= \frac{1}{\abs{a}} \cd \frac{1}{\sdpar\sqrt{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{\paren{(y-b)/a - \mean}^2}{2\ss}}
&& \text{(Gaussian density of } X \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\abs{a}\sdpar\sqrt{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{\paren{(y-b-a\mean)/a}^2}{2\ss}}
&& \text{(common denominator } a \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\abs{a}\sdpar\sqrt{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{(y-(a\mean+b))^2}{2a^2\ss}}
&& \text{(} (u/a)^2 = u^2/a^2 \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2\ss}\sqrt{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{(y-(a\mean+b))^2}{2a^2\ss}}
&& \text{(} \abs{a}\sdpar = \sqrt{a^2\ss} \text{)}
\ea
$$

This is the density of $\ndist{a\mean + b, a^2\ss}$ with mean parameter $a\mean + b$ and variance parameter $a^2\ss > 0$.

:::
